messages:
jess.sales: Heads-up: HelixMed wants a short, prescriptive Private deployment runbook for their security review. Key asks: PrivateLink only (peering blocked), audit-quality client IPs in logs, strict outbound firewall rules, and cost breakdown for the POC.

ravi.se: Understood. PrivateLink is fine but it doesn't give raw client IP to our service. We usually recommend header propagation (X-Forwarded-For) from a customer-side proxy or a mutual-TLS proxy to carry identity.

ops.maria: Quick notes from networking: 
- PrivateLink traffic shows the interface endpoint ENI as source on our side. We can match that ENI back to the customer, but not the original pod/client IP unless they forward it.
- If they cannot run a proxy, alternative is to terminate TLS in their VPC and forward requests; that preserves an application-level header.

claire.cs: They mentioned long-lived inference streams (gRPC); will header forwarding work for that?

ravi.se: Yes. For gRPC we pass XFF as metadata if their proxy adds it. If they use TLS passthrough to our ALB/NLB, then the connection is TCP-level and you still see endpoint ENI IPs. For HTTP/2/gRPC with proxy termination, headers are preserved.

jess.sales: Security team asks for explicit SG rule snippets and a minimal runbook page they can attach to the questionnaire. Can we include an SG example plus a small checklist?

ops.maria: SG snippet for their endpoint side (customer VPC):

- Inbound: allow app client CIDR -> TCP 443 (app frontends)
- Outbound: allow TCP 443 -> destination: our PrivateLink endpoint ENI security group (we will provide SG id)
- Outbound: UDP/TCP 53 -> VPC Resolver (if they do DNS lookups)
- Outbound: UDP 123 only if they require NTP to an external server

And on our side: endpoint SG only allows inbound from that customer endpoint SG. We'll request the SG ID during provisioning.

ravi.se: Additions to runbook:
1) Create Interface Endpoint in customer account for service:com.redwood.private.<region> in each AZ they need.
2) Attach endpoint to private subnet with route to NAT or IGW as per their design (note: endpoint ENIs are in-place and do not route through NAT).
3) Set endpoint SG to permit outbound to the service and inbound from app clients.
4) Deploy a tiny proxy (Envoy/nginx) in the customer's app subnet to terminate TLS and append X-Forwarded-For. Example envoy config will be provided.
5) Validate with: curl -k -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.10.4' https://service.internal/health and check logs in Redwood to see the XFF line.

claire.cs: For the questionnaire, add an FAQ: Why not VPC Peering/TGW? -> peering would preserve src IP but requires cross-account route acceptance and opens subnet-level routes between accounts; customer's policy forbids that. PrivateLink provides a narrower attack surface.

ops.maria: Other operational caveats to document:
- MTU: PrivateLink can reduce effective MTU; recommend enabling MSS clamping on any customer NAT/proxy.
- IP allowlisting: we can provide the endpoint private ENI IPs for the POC, but they can change if endpoints are recreated. Prefer SG-based allow rules.
- Cross-AZ: If endpoint is in different AZ than backend, expect small latency bump (~2-6ms).

jess.sales: Pricing note for the quote: include PrivateLink per-hour endpoint cost + data processing per GB + our Private deployment monthly charge. HelixMed expects a 5TB/month example.

ops.maria: Rough numbers to use in the POC: endpoint cost ~ $0.015/hr per AZ (region dependent), data processing ~ $0.01/GB. For 5TB inbound traffic thatstimates to ~$50 for data processing + endpoint hours (~$11/AZ/month). I'll refine for their region. Also note egress to internet (if any) would be billed separately.

sec-bot: Automated: update S-14 network_architecture in the security questionnaire with the PrivateLink diagram and attach SG snippets after runbook finalised.

jess.sales: Action items:
- ravi.se: produce a 1-page runbook + envoy/nginx sample config and XFF example.
- ops.maria: finalize cost numbers for 5TB/month and provide POC endpoint IPs/SG (best-effort) for the region.
- claire.cs: confirm with HelixMed whether they will run proxy and accept XFF or require mTLS.

ravi.se: I'll drop the runbook and sample config into the shared drive and ping when ready.

ops.maria: I'll send a cost line-item spreadsheet by EOD PT.

jess.sales: Thanks everyone. I'll schedule a 45-min technical handoff with HelixMed for Friday 10am PT and include the runbook.

claire.cs: I'll join the call.

jess.sales: Closing thread for now — will reopen if the security team has follow-up. :white_check_mark:
